changelog: - **One notification router, one typed event catalogue and a per-recipient delivery ledger** (#1710). Notifications fanned out per feature: each send site picked its own event string, decided on its own whether an e-mail went with the in-app row, and reached for whichever preference helper its author remembered — and "was the mentor actually told, on which channel?" had no answer anywhere. `src/lib/notifications/catalog.ts` now carries one typed entry per event (all 102 `notifications.events` keys) with its notification category, e-mail group, default channels, `immediate|batched` delivery mode, link kind and declared template placeholders, and `notifyEvent(recipients, eventKey, payload)` in `src/lib/notifications/router.ts` resolves recipient → locale → preferences → channels → ledger row → channel. An unknown event key and a payload missing a placeholder are both compile errors (`typeContract.ts` asserts that with `@ts-expect-error`, which `tsc --noEmit` fails when the mistake stops being one), and `scripts/test/notification-catalog.test.mjs` fails when a dictionary key has no catalogue entry, an entry has no template, or a template's placeholders drift from the declared payload **in any one of the three locales** — the failure that renders a literal `{name}` to German readers only. The new `NotificationDelivery` model is one row per (recipient, event, channel): `QUEUED|SENT|SKIPPED|FAILED` with a `skipReason`, `orgId` stamped from the recipient's own row and registered in `TENANT_MODELS`, and a non-null globally-unique `dedupeKey` (nullable unique columns de-duplicate nothing in MySQL — the trap already documented on `Job.idempotencyKey`) so a retried send neither duplicates the row nor sends twice. The preference check runs **before** the row is claimed, which is the opposite of the dormant-first-contact sweep's recorded mistake of spending a person's mail quota on mail that was never sent. `notifyEvent` never throws and never blocks the caller's transaction: every step degrades to a log. Nothing is migrated in this change — the existing `notify()` keeps its exact in-app-only behaviour and is re-exported from the router as the shim its existing call sites move through, and the e-mail channel enqueues a durable `notification.email` job rather than sending inline (its handler arrives with the queue worker).
